strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across two domains (speech and music) with rigorous human evaluation methodology (50 raters × 50 samples, Bradley-Terry statistical modeling)
Demonstrates practical value: significant inference speedups (1.3-2.2× overall, 5.4-19.3× sampler speedup for quality-competitive models) while maintaining or improving audio fidelity
Thorough ablation studies (Table 5) clearly demonstrate the necessity of each component, with detailed analysis of failure modes
Well-motivated approach combining noise-robustness for long-term modeling with clean short-context local information
Comprehensive hyperparameter documentation and implementation details enabling reproducibility
Multiple evaluation metrics (objective: FAD, MOSNet, ABX, PPX, VERT; subjective: acoustic quality, meaningfulness/enjoyment) with confidence intervals
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (VAE from Evans et al., consistency models from Lu & Song, noise injection from Pasini et al., short-context transformer similar to DiTAR) rather than introducing new methods

Critical missing comparisons: No direct experimental comparison with SALAD (Turetzky et al. 2024) and DiTAR (Jia et al. 2025)—the most relevant continuous-latent audio baselines—despite citing them extensively

Misleading speedup claims: Headline speedups (×19.3 sampler) are for 1-step generation with lower quality (FAD 0.83). Practical quality-competitive speedup is ×5.4 (4-step, FAD 0.71 vs baseline 1.06), a distinction insufficiently highlighted

Fragility of base approach: Table 5 ablation shows catastrophic failure when removing short-context transformer (FAD 4.03) or noise augmentation (FAD 1.63), suggesting the model requires careful engineering and may lack robustness
Unclear VAE efficiency advantage: Requires 96-128 latent dimensions to match 32-level RVQ quality (Table 3). No computational cost analysis of VAE encoding/decoding versus RVQ on actual systems

Architectural inconsistency undermines generality: Speech and music use fundamentally different architectures (speech lacks noise augmentation and short-context transformer), raising questions about method generalization
Lack of reproducibility resources: No mention of code availability, model weights, or complete audio sample links despite being critical for a venue expecting reproducible research

Incomplete comparisons for music: Required retraining MusicGen on CALM's dataset rather than using official models; only 400K songs from LAION-Disco-12M; no semantic distillation for music VAE (acknowledged as future work)

Gaussian temperature sampling is ad-hoc: Acknowledges Jacobian term is 'untractable' and applies temperature only to noise sampling without theoretical justification—a workaround rather than principled solution
Limited scalability analysis: Only tested at 1.3B vs 3B parameters on music only; authors state 'complete scalability study for future work' weakening confidence in scalability claims

strengths: Well-motivated problem articulation: clearly explains the quality-computation trade-off in discrete quantization and provides genuine motivation for continuous alternatives
Comprehensive experimental methodology with both objective metrics and human evaluation across two domains (speech and music) with 50 participants × 50 samples
Strong empirical results: consistent improvements over RQ-Transformer baselines with significant inference speedups (12.3× speech, 19.3× music) and improved human ratings
Solid ablation studies demonstrating component importance (Table 5 shows critical role of short-context transformer with 4.3× FAD degradation when removed)
Good reproducibility practices with extensive hyperparameter documentation and promised code release; detailed architectural specifications
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: core components (VAE codec, consistency models, noise injection, short-context transformer) are from prior work; primary contribution is combining existing techniques without fundamental new insights

Gaussian temperature sampling lacks theoretical justification: authors acknowledge Jacobian term is 'intractable' and provide only a heuristic approximation without principled derivation; evaluation only on speaker diversity, not audio quality

Experimental fairness concerns: RQ-Transformer baselines appear custom-trained with unclear tuning effort; speech model uses 'inner monologue' semantic guidance potentially giving unfair advantage; no direct comparison with closely related Pasini et al. (2024b) or DiTAR

Incomplete scalability evaluation: only one 3B model tested in appendix; authors explicitly state 'we leave a complete scalability study for future work,' undermining claims of state-of-the-art generalization

Limited metric diversity for music: FAD is primary objective metric; additional metrics (CLAP, timbral assessments) would strengthen quality claims; human evaluation sample size modest (50 samples) with no inter-rater reliability reported
Unclear VAE training details: which components from Mimi are used vs. modified? What is the training data scale? Independent VAE quality evaluation missing
No failure mode analysis: paper lacks discussion of when CALM underperforms, when error accumulation occurs, or diagnostic experiments on why VAE outperforms discrete approaches

Presentation scattered between speech/music results making holistic assessment difficult; key details (scalability, hyperparameters) relegated to appendix; unclear technical distinctions with related work (Pasini et al., DiTAR)
Head batch multiplier is straightforward training trick (reusing computed context with multiple noise samples) rather than methodological contribution
Table 6 (consistency vs. TrigFlow) merely shows speed-quality tradeoff, not fundamental superiority of consistency modeling for this task

strengths: Strong empirical results across speech and music domains, outperforming discrete baselines on both quality metrics (FAD, MOSNet, ABX) and human evaluation while achieving 12-19× sampler speedup
Comprehensive experimental methodology including thorough ablations (Table 5), human evaluation with 50 raters, multiple automatic metrics, and appropriate baselines
Well-motivated problem addressing the quality-efficiency tradeoff of discrete audio tokens, with practical solutions that enable 1-step generation
First successful application of continuous autoregressive latent modeling to music generation, extending prior work beyond text-to-speech

Effective combination of architectural innovations: noise-injected long-term context + clean short-term context enables significant quality improvements (ablation: 0.93 vs 4.03 FAD without short-context)
Good reproducibility: extensive hyperparameter details, multiple evaluation metrics, proper statistical reporting with confidence intervals
Demonstrates scalability with 3B backbone experiments showing continued improvements over 1.3B baseline
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (VAE from Evans et al./Mimi, noise injection from Pasini et al., consistency models from Lu & Song 2025, short-context transformer inspired by DiTAR) rather than introducing fundamentally new methods

Gaussian temperature sampling lacks theoretical justification: authors acknowledge ignoring the Jacobian determinant and justify only by empirical observation ('we noticed'), undermining the principled nature of the approach

Narrow evaluation scope limits generalizability: speech only evaluated on continuation with inner monologue (somewhat orthogonal to CALM), music only on 30-second sequences with no evaluation of longer-context or unconditional generation
Incomplete scalability analysis: Section A.2 provides only single 3B experiment; authors explicitly defer 'complete scalability study for future work'; modest gains shown (13% improvement 1.3B→3B)

Insufficient analysis of design choices: unclear why short-context transformer provides massive performance gain (ablation shows 4.03→0.93 FAD), why naive MAR fails, or what each component learns without attention visualization or deeper investigation

Missing comparisons: Table 6 shows TrigFlow achieves significantly better quality (0.64 FAD at 100 steps vs 2.05 consistency) but positioned only as speed tradeoff; recent shortcut model baselines (Hang et al. 2025) acknowledged but not compared

Limited scope for speech experiments: inner monologue mechanism feels orthogonal to CALM core contribution and would work with discrete models; evaluation limited to guided continuation rather than unconditional generation
Reproducibility limitations: music trained on proprietary LAION subset (400K songs), speech on proprietary French/English data; code availability not mentioned

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across 4 diverse audio tasks with both objective metrics and human evaluation
Strong practical results: Pocket TTS achieves 100M parameters with competitive performance (WER 1.84) faster than real-time on CPU
Substantial inference speedups (×12-20 for sampling head via consistency models) with maintained or improved quality
Thorough ablation studies (Table 5) clearly demonstrating importance of each component, particularly the short-context transformer
Excellent reproducibility documentation with detailed hyperparameters, architecture specifications, and promised code release
Well-motivated problem formulation addressing genuine trade-offs in discrete audio quantization
Clear architectural design combining noise-robust long-term and clean short-term context
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (consistency models from Lu & Song 2025, LSD from Boffi et al. 2025, short-context from DiTAR, noise injection from Pasini et al. 2024b) rather than introducing new methods

Evaluation reliability concerns: automatic speaker similarity metric (0.52) contradicts human evaluation results where all methods beat ground truth (>1900 Elo); authors acknowledge as 'surprising' but provide no adequate explanation

Incomplete scalability analysis: only tested up to 3B parameters with admission that 'complete scalability study left for future work'; no analysis of degradation over long sequences despite being a stated motivation
Gaussian temperature sampling presented as heuristic (σ→√τ) without theoretical justification or thorough empirical validation of effectiveness compared to discrete temperature sampling

Presentation density: attempting to cover 4 tasks with multiple models dilutes focus; primary contributions sometimes unclear; important details relegated to appendix

strengths: Clear motivation addressing genuine limitation of discrete quantization in audio generation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 4 diverse audio tasks (speech/music, conditional/unconditional) with broad scope
Strong empirical results: 2.2× speedup with improved FAD on music, better metrics on speech tasks, Pocket TTS achieves real-time CPU performance
Thorough ablation studies effectively demonstrating component importance, particularly short-context transformer's criticality
Well-motivated practical contributions: head batch multiplier, Gaussian temperature sampling, latent CFG
Excellent reproducibility: comprehensive hyperparameter tables, hyperparameter search details, code release commitment
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (MAR, consistency models, noise injection from prior work); short-context transformer is relatively simple contribution

Critical metric reliability failure: Table 3 shows WavLM speaker similarity produces counterintuitive results (0.52 vs 0.57 for reference), suggesting metric unreliability; resorting to human evaluation undermines confidence in other automatic metrics throughout paper

Unfair comparisons: parameter counts not consistently reported across baselines; total CALM capacity (backbone 1.35B + short-context 113M + head 601M) vs RQ-Transformer comparison unclear; some baselines from closed-source papers rather than direct implementations

Fundamental task-dependent architecture design: authors state no gains from noise injection or short-context for speech continuation (contradicting music results); architecture differs significantly across tasks, suggesting method is not a unified general solution but task-specific engineering

Incomplete analysis of improvement sources: unclear whether gains come from continuous latents vs. VAE-GAN codec quality vs. consistency models vs. short-context; missing critical ablation of RQ-Transformer with same codec to isolate architectural improvements
LSD vs. Consistency contradiction: Table E.5 shows LSD provides better quality than Consistency at ~300M scale, yet paper emphasizes consistency models without explaining this preference

Quality-speed tradeoff concerns: Table 9 reveals TrigFlow achieves FAD 0.64 vs Consistency's 2.05 at 100 steps (3.2× degradation); paper treats this as solved but for many non-streaming applications, quality should be prioritized
Pocket TTS improvements conflate multiple factors: speedup from both distillation and consistency modeling; unclear separation of contribution from continuous modeling specifically

Vague design justifications: temperature sampling heuristic lacks rigor, latent CFG is non-standard without theoretical justification, VAE differences between speech/music unexplained (semantic distillation deferred to future work)

Limited analysis of method sensitivity and failure modes: no discussion of VAE quality sensitivity, generalization to other audio domains, or edge cases; preliminary scalability study (E.4) lacks depth
Task-specific parameter sensitivity: ablation shows huge sensitivity to architecture (FAD 0.71→4.03 without short-context), yet this component is inconsistently beneficial across tasks

strengths: Well-motivated problem articulation addressing fundamental quality-computation tradeoff of discrete RVQ approaches
Comprehensive technical approach combining multiple well-justified innovations (dual-transformer architecture, 1-step consistency models, temperature sampling, head batch multiplier)
Extensive experimental validation across 4 audio tasks with rigorous evaluation: automatic metrics, human studies (50 samples × 50 raters), ablations (Table 5), and scalability analysis

Strong empirical results: 2.2× overall speedup and 19.3× sampler speedup for music, 12.3× for speech, improved quality scores, outperforms RQ-Transformer and recent baselines (F5-TTS, DSM, SALAD, DiTAR)
Practical impact with Pocket TTS: 100M-parameter model achieving faster-than-realtime CPU inference while maintaining competitive quality
Excellent reproducibility: complete hyperparameters (Tables 13-14), comprehensive appendices with supplementary experiments, promised code release, detailed experimental protocols
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: primarily combines existing components (MAR, noise injection from Pasini et al., consistency models from Lu & Song, short-context design similar to DiTAR) without fundamental innovations

Incremental conceptual advance over prior continuous audio work: SALAD and DiTAR already showed continuous models work for speech/TTS; paper extends to music and improves efficiency but lacks novel insights distinguishing CALM from scaling prior approaches

Gaussian temperature sampling (Section 4.5) presented as heuristic without theoretical justification; empirically validated at τ=0.8 with no analysis of sensitivity, failure modes, or why this approximation preserves desired properties

Short-context transformer design insufficiently justified: ablation confirms importance but hypothesis on why noisy long-term + clean short-term outperforms alternatives (Section 4.3) is speculative with no controlled experiments on noise levels

VAE design choices underexplored: inconsistent design (VAE-GAN for speech vs. plain VAE for music); Table 7 shows VAE requires 96-128 dims to match 32-RVQ quality, unclear if truly advantageous; no comparison with alternative continuous encoders

Speaker similarity metric anomaly (Table 3): CALM gets 0.52 while ground truth VAE gets 0.57, suggesting metric issues; human evaluation suggests metric doesn't capture intended signal but unresolved explanation
Limited scalability analysis: only one scale-up experiment (1.3B→3B backbone); no systematic curves; acknowledged future work; unclear if consistency remains optimal at larger scales

TrigFlow vs. consistency tradeoff underdeveloped: Table 4 shows TrigFlow achieves better FAD (0.64 vs 0.71) but slower; Table 9 partially addresses but no Pareto frontier analysis or hybrid strategies explored
Minimal failure mode analysis: no discussion of when/why CALM diverges, quality degradation over long sequences, or task-specific challenges

Experimental scope limitations: music uses single internal LAION subset with generalization unclear; text-to-music main results on internal dataset; text-to-speech uses different preprocessing (Adobe Enhance) between CALM and baselines, raising fairness concerns
